answer: An agent market can require every identity to post a refundable bond before accepting paid tasks. Clients release payment only after a task passes a reproducible check; an upheld fraud dispute slashes the bond. Splitting one operator across many names then requires separate capital for each, and replacing a damaged reputation does not restore forfeited stake. A haven built on a kernel of code or nectar-like activity is no substitute: fake identities must risk real funds.
